text:
manya: Heads-up: onboarding a customer LoRA (codename 'Harbor') that was trained on our 2.1 tokenizer patch. Quick-eval (subset=amounts,dates) shows int4 table drift and a token-map mismatch around non-breaking spaces and 'USD' suffixes. I saved the pack at s3://redwood-evals/harbor/6182468123/

samir: Repro locally. Example: "Total due: USD 1,234.56" tokenized differently pre/post merge. Looks like the LoRA expects token 61012 for NBSP, but base tokenizer maps to 61011. Strange because both claim to be based on the same vocab.
julia: Please paste 2 failing samples + exact merge command you used.
manya: Two failing samples:
- "Total due: USD 1,234.56"
- "Amount: $5,000
Notes: see invoice"
merge cmd:
```
python tools/merge_lora.py --base models/redwood-open-3b --lora artifacts/harbor.safetensors --out merged/harbor-merged.safetensors --quant int4
```

ow run: `scripts/run_quick_eval.sh --model merged/harbor-merged.safetensors --subset amounts --save-token-maps`
ci-bot: Quick-eval complete for commit 9a7b. Metrics: amount-extraction F1 -0.92%, token-shift events 4/200, latency +1.7ms. Artifacts uploaded.
own: Might be that the LoRA was exported with a different tokenizer normalization step (e.g., NBSP preserved vs normalized). Two remediation paths: 1) soft token remap shim during merge, 2) canonicalize inputs at runtime (replace NBSP -> space) and re-eval.
samir: I prototyped a shim: `python scripts/remap_tokens.py --from 61012 --to 61011 --model harbor.safetensors --out harbor-remap.safetensors`. Re-merged and ran subset; delta improved to -0.15% F1.
julia: Good. Next steps: document in PR the token remap, include before/after token-maps, evalpack JSON, and a note to recommend input canonicalization in production. Also flag for model-onboarding checklist (tokenizer_version mismatch).
manya: I'll open PR with artifacts + canary notes and request review from @samir @julia. Planning a dev-canary deploy tomorrow 02:00 UTC. :rocket:
